questions.question: What is the difference between demand and quantity demanded?
questions.reference_answer: Demand is the relationship across prices and quantities, represented by a demand curve or schedule. Quantity demanded is the specific quantity at one particular price, a point on that curve or schedule.

questions.question: At the current price, buyers want more than sellers offer. Why does the price tend to rise?
questions.retrieval_query: shortage excess demand quantity demanded supplied price equilibrium
questions.reference_answer: A price below equilibrium produces a shortage: quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied. Sellers can sell their available goods at a higher price, so the price rises toward equilibrium.

questions.question: What does price elasticity of demand measure?
questions.retrieval_query: price elasticity demand percentage change quantity demanded price
questions.reference_answer: Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity demanded divided by the corresponding percentage change in price. It measures the responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change.

questions.question: How does raising price affect total revenue when demand is elastic versus inelastic?
questions.retrieval_query: elastic inelastic demand price total revenue
questions.reference_answer: Total revenue equals price times quantity sold. With elastic demand, a price increase causes a larger percentage decrease in quantity, reducing revenue. With inelastic demand, the smaller percentage quantity decrease means revenue rises. With unit elasticity, moderate price changes leave revenue unchanged.
